description: Add a pure control-plane range-invalidation workflow action `rerun-from-stage` that resumes a run from any stage it has already reached, delivered end-to-end through domain → grain → HTTP API, plus the parallel `mo issue rerun-from-stage` CLI command.

tasks.title: Implement rerun-from-stage control action (domain + grain + HTTP API) with tests
tasks.description: Deliver the server-side `rerun-from-stage` capability as a single cohesive vertical slice mirroring the existing `rerun` pattern. Add the validate-and-mutate domain method `RerunFromStage(stageId)` to the `extension(WorkflowRun run)` block in WorkflowRun.Failure.cs (alongside `Rerun()`), a typed `WorkflowControlRejectionException(Code, Message, Details)` for actionable rejections, the `RerunFromStageAsync(stageId)` grain method (mutate → release range locks → CommitAsync), and the `POST /{number}/rerun-from-stage` route with DTO + error mapping. Later stages reuse the existing lazy InitializeFreshStagesAsync + Advance path; no new event types or persisted fields. Follow design.md decisions D1–D7 exactly.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain `RerunFromStage(stageId)` replaces the target stage with a new StageRun (same Id, Attempt = old+1, Initialized=false, empty tasks/checks, Status=Running, RequiresApproval copied) and every later stage with a fresh StageRun (same Id, Attempt=1, Initialized=false, empty tasks/checks, Status=Pending); stages before the target are byte-for-byte untouched.
Domain method sets CurrentStageId = target stage Id, clears run.Failure, sets run.Status = Running, and returns exactly [WorkflowRunResumed, StageStarted(target)].
Domain method rejects unknown stage id by throwing the typed exception with code `unknown_stage` BEFORE any mutation; run.Stages, CurrentStageId, Failure, and Status remain unchanged.

Domain method rejects a never-reached stage (position strictly ahead of current) with code `stage_not_reached`, and the exception Details include `eligibleStages` (ids with index <= current index); no state mutated.

Domain method rejects when ANY stage in [targetIdx..end] holds a non-terminal task (Pending/Running) or a Pending/Running check with code `active_work_in_range` and a message instructing to stop/cancel first; no state mutated.
Runtime variables scoped to the run are preserved across the operation (domain test asserts pre-existing run variables remain and the target's new attempt can read them).

Grain `RerunFromStageAsync(stageId)` calls EnsureRun → `_run.RerunFromStage(stageId)` (which throws on rejection) → iterates Stages[targetIdx..end] calling ReleaseStageLocksAsync(stage.Id, "rerun-from-stage") → CommitAsync(events); no lock release and no CommitAsync on the rejection path.

Grain test verifies the target stage is Initialized in the same commit as the emitted StageStarted(target), and that a later stage is lazily initialized from the current template only when advance reaches it (mirror StageInitEagerSpecs.Rerun_RestartsStage_StageInitializedInSameCommit).

Grain test verifies a sequential stage lock held within the target-to-end range is released on success, a lock for a stage before the target is NOT released, and an active running task in a later stage causes the operation to be rejected (no lock released, state unchanged).

HTTP `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/{number}/rerun-from-stage` returns 200 on a valid request whose stage was reached and has no active work in range; body DTO is `RerunFromStageRequest(string? Stage)`.

HTTP route returns 400 for empty/whitespace/missing `stage` (validated at the route before the grain call); 400 with `eligibleStages` details for `unknown_stage`/`stage_not_reached`; 409 for `active_work_in_range`; 404 when the issue has no workflow run; keeps the IsWorkflowRunStateCorruption self-heal catch for parity with /rerun.

HTTP route reuses WorkflowControlAction.RetryOrRerun eligibility (failed/active controllable states), so archived/completed issues return a conflict — verified by adding `rerun-from-stage` to the existing [Theory] InlineData sets in IssueArchivedDetailApiSpecs.cs.

New HTTP integration tests (mirroring WorkflowRetrySessionHealthGuardSpecs.cs) cover 200 success, 400 empty stage, 400 never-reached stage (assert eligibleStages), 409 active-work, and 404 no-workflow-run.
Existing retry and rerun behavior is unchanged: all existing retry/rerun domain, grain, and API tests pass without modification.
`dotnet build Mohist.sln` succeeds with TreatWarningsAsErrors and `npm test` (server test suite) passes.
No new event types, no new persisted field on WorkflowRun/StageRun, no persistence migration, no change to WorkflowStatusMapper.BuildAvailableActions (deferred per design Open Question).
tasks.output: Server implementation: WorkflowRun.Failure.cs (RerunFromStage), new WorkflowControlRejectionException, IWorkflowGrain.cs + WorkflowGrain.cs (RerunFromStageAsync), IssueRoutes.WorkflowControl.cs (route + DTO), plus domain/grain/API test files; green `npm test` for server.
tasks.notes: Exception placement: design D4 says mirror the WorkflowSessionContextExhaustedException precedent; since the domain method throws it, place it in a namespace the domain layer can reference without inversion (the precedent lives under Workflow/Grains/ — keep the new exception alongside it only if the domain project already references that namespace, otherwise place it under Workflow/Domain/). Emit only WorkflowRunResumed + StageStarted(target); the existing CommitAsync → InitializeFreshStagesAsync loop handles target init and later-stage lazy init. Lock release is idempotent so iterating the whole range is safe.

tasks.title: Implement `mo issue rerun-from-stage` CLI command with tests
tasks.description: Add the user-facing `mo issue rerun-from-stage <number> --stage <id>` subcommand parallel to `issue retry`/`issue rerun`, using a dedicated builder (modeled on BuildReject, NOT the body-less BuildAction) because it must send a `{ stage }` body. It resolves the project, validates the required --stage option, POSTs to the rerun-from-stage endpoint delivered by T-001, and surfaces server-provided code+message on actionable errors.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo issue rerun-from-stage <number> --stage build` resolves the project id and POSTs `{ "stage": "build" }` to `/api/projects/<projectId>/issues/<number>/rerun-from-stage` (verified via a recording HTTP handler asserting the exact path and JSON body).
Running `mo issue rerun-from-stage <number>` without `--stage` prints a usage error to stderr and makes NO HTTP request (returns non-zero exit code).
Server-provided error code and message (e.g. active_work_in_range conflict, stage_not_reached bad request) surface to the user via the existing PrintResponseAsync path.
The command advertises `--project`/`--project-id` options (shares MohistCliCommands.ProjectRefOption), matching the project-resolution conventions of reject/stop.
`rerun-from-stage` is added to the CLI project-ref [Theory] in IssueCliRemainingProjectRefSpecs.cs so --project/--project-id are advertised in --help.
New CLI spec (mirroring CliIssueRejectAndStopSpecs.cs) covers: successful POST body shape, missing --stage usage error, and project-id alias resolution.

`dotnet build Mohist.sln` succeeds with TreatWarningsAsErrors and CLI tests pass (CLI is a .NET project covered by `npm test` / `dotnet test Mohist.sln`; there is no `packages/cli` npm workspace); existing retry/rerun CLI behavior is unchanged.
tasks.output: CLI implementation: BuildRerunFromStage in MohistCliCommands.Issue.cs + registration in Build(), plus a new CliIssueRerunFromStageSpecs.cs test file and updates to IssueCliRemainingProjectRefSpecs.cs; green CLI tests.
tasks.notes: Use a dedicated builder (like BuildReject at MohistCliCommands.Issue.cs:587), not BuildAction, because the command carries a required --stage option and a JSON body. Print via api.PrintPostAsync(path, new { stage }) per design D6; do not add --output handling unless matching BuildReject's output flow.
